Cursor launched Projects in beta on September 10 for people building a personal website or app. A Project keeps the files and notes for one longer job. A coordinator is the agent that plans the job and sends pieces to other agents; Cursor says the other agents write the code.

A Project runs on a computer in the cloud—online rather than on your laptop—so closing your laptop does not stop that part of the job. If testing is needed on your own computer, Cursor says the coordinator starts a local agent there. The result comes back to you to check.

[P002] Cursor launched Projects in beta on September 10 for people building a personal website or app. A Project keeps the files and notes for one longer job. A coordinator is the agent that plans the job and sends pieces to other agents; Cursor says the other agents write the code. [P003] A Project runs on a computer in the cloud—online rather than on your laptop—so closing your laptop does not stop that part of the job. If testing is needed on your own computer, Cursor says the coordinator starts a local agent there. The result comes back to you to check. [P004] For a simple website-page job, that could mean letting cloud agents work on the page after you shut your laptop. If the job needs testing on your computer, it is a different handoff. The useful question before you start is: will this job stay online, or does it need my own computer for testing? [P005] Projects are in beta and rolling out to all users. [P006] When the page comes back, check the thing you asked for: does it say what you meant, do its links work, and did anything else change? That is the concrete job that still belongs to you. When something needs testing on your machine, the coordinator spins up a local agent to run it there.\nYou shouldn't have to onboard an agent every time you start a task. Agents add research and artifacts, along with what they learn about the codebase and how you prefer work to be done. If one agent figures out how to test a service, for example, every future agent can use those instructions.
